item.title: Allow backyard cottages near frequent transit

background.name: Planning and Development
background.publisher: City of Houston Planning and Development Department

item.summary: Let homeowners add one small rental home on eligible residential lots near transit. Keep existing safety standards and publish a clear permit checklist.
item.currentText: An additional dwelling requires a separate discretionary review.
item.proposedText: Permit one accessory dwelling on eligible lots within a half-mile of frequent transit, subject to building and fire codes.

item.title: Cap childcare copays for working families

background.name: Office of Child Care
background.publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Administration for Children and Families
background.scope: Federal child care program background only

item.summary: Limit eligible families’ childcare copays and fund providers to cover the difference. Publish enrollment and wait-list measures each quarter.
item.currentText: Family copays vary by program and eligibility category.
item.proposedText: Limit participating families’ childcare copays to 7 percent of household income and reimburse eligible providers for the difference.

item.title: Run frequent buses on evenings and weekends

background.name: METRO
background.publisher: Metropolitan Transit Authority of Harris County
background.scope: Regional transit agency background only; not a city bill

item.summary: Pilot 15-minute bus service on three high-demand corridors until 10 p.m. Measure missed trips, access to jobs, and ridership before expanding.
item.currentText: Evening and weekend service follows the existing lower-frequency schedule.
item.proposedText: Fund a twelve-month pilot of fifteen-minute service through 10 p.m. on three priority corridors, with quarterly public reporting.

item.title: Prioritize drainage work around repeatedly flooded homes
item.summary: Rank drainage projects by repeat flooding, household vulnerability, and expected risk reduction. Publish the ranking and progress every quarter.
item.currentText: Drainage projects are scheduled through the existing capital improvement process.
item.proposedText: Publish a risk-based drainage priority list and reserve a portion of annual capital funding for repeatedly flooded neighborhoods.

item.title: Publish the full price before routine medical care
item.summary: Give patients an understandable cost estimate before scheduled care. Include facility and clinician charges and explain how to dispute a surprise bill.
item.currentText: Patients may receive separate estimates for facility and clinician services.
item.proposedText: Require a single plain-language estimate for scheduled services, including known facility and clinician charges and a dispute contact.

item.title: Make school crossings safer before the next school year

background.name: Vision Zero Houston
background.scope: City street safety initiative background only

item.summary: Improve twenty high-risk school crossings with visible markings, shorter crossings, and accessible signals. Publish before-and-after speed and safety data.
item.currentText: School crossing upgrades compete within the general street maintenance queue.
item.proposedText: Create a dedicated school crossing program prioritizing twenty high-risk locations, with accessible design and published completion dates.

item.title: Bring affordable groceries to underserved neighborhoods

background.name: Food Access Research Atlas
background.publisher: U.S. Department of Agriculture, Economic Research Service
background.scope: Federal food access data background; not evidence of a county pilot

item.summary: Pilot weekly mobile grocery stops and discounted delivery in neighborhoods with limited supermarket access. Track household reach and the price of a basic basket.
item.currentText: Existing food access programs do not guarantee regular grocery service in every priority area.
item.proposedText: Fund a one-year mobile grocery pilot with weekly stops in priority areas and public reporting on affordability and household reach.

item.title: Offer a first mental health appointment within two weeks
item.summary: Expand community clinic appointments and telehealth referrals. Track time to first appointment while protecting patient privacy.
item.currentText: Community mental health appointment availability varies by provider and region.
item.proposedText: Fund additional community clinic capacity with a target of a first appointment within fourteen days and quarterly aggregate wait-time reporting.

item.title: Give small businesses one clear permit checklist
item.summary: Combine routine startup permits into one checklist and show the current status of each step. Publish typical processing times and a help contact.
item.currentText: Applicants navigate separate department checklists and status updates.
item.proposedText: Provide a consolidated startup permit checklist, shared status tracking, and published service targets for routine applications.

item.title: Explain property insurance increases before renewal
item.summary: Require a clear explanation of major premium changes and coverage differences before renewal. Give households time to compare options.
item.currentText: Renewal notices list premiums and policy terms in separate documents.
item.proposedText: Provide a plain-language renewal comparison showing premium changes, deductibles, coverage reductions, and consumer assistance contacts.

item.title: Add shade at the hottest bus stops

background.name: City of Houston
background.scope: City homepage only; does not substantiate bus stop heat or shelter claims

item.summary: Install shade and seating at high-use bus stops with the greatest heat exposure. Prioritize riders with limited mobility and publish a maintenance schedule.
item.currentText: Bus stop shelter placement follows the existing amenity program.
item.proposedText: Prioritize shade and accessible seating at high-ridership, high-heat stops and publish annual installation and maintenance targets.

item.title: Show residents where each budget dollar goes

background.name: Harris County
background.scope: County homepage only; does not substantiate budget dashboard claims

item.summary: Publish a searchable budget with project spending and milestones. Make the data downloadable and explain changes in plain English.
item.currentText: Budget and project spending reports are published in separate documents.
item.proposedText: Publish a searchable, accessible budget dashboard linking approved spending to project milestones, with monthly downloadable updates.
